text:
emily-support: FYI — CS just escalated ACME: persistent 503s during streaming toolcall (high QPS). Root logs on the infer worker look like an abort + GPU OOM then segfault. Need triage and quick mitigation, customer on a call in 20m.

emily-support: logs (snip):
```
[15:01:21] runner[pid=4217]: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory (alloc 1.2GiB)
[15:01:21] runner[pid=4217]: attempting oom fallback -> evict pages
[15:01:22] runner[pid=4217]: SIGSEGV at 0x7f9b2c1f4c
[15:01:22] infer-daemon: exit code 139, restart triggered
[15:01:22] gateway: upstream 503 from infer-worker-7 (retries exhausted)
```

mike-sre: Thanks — how many customers impacted besides ACME? Can you paste per-second 5xx rate + worker restart count for the last 10m? Also did fallback routing kick to smaller model or CPU pool?

emily-support: Only ACME so far (their traffic is high). 5xx spike started ~15:00 UTC, ~120 req/min to that worker pool; restart count +3 in last 5m. Fallback didn't trigger — routing policy prefers same-model variants and no CPU fallback configured for this pool.

raj-infra: I can see the node metrics — GPU memory climbed steadily and then a sharp drop on restart. There's a KV-prefetch memory regression in qps-heavy embed/streaming cases we've been tracking. Correlates with a recent rollout of kselector v2 earlier today.

carla-eng: Noted — kselector v2 changed some ordering for attention kernels which can increase staging allocation in certain quant paths. We rolled it at 14:40 to staging then to prod at 14:55. Will investigate if that interaction causes transient over-alloc.

ops-oncall: Short-term mitigation suggestions: 1) reduce max_batch_size for the pool 2) disable KV prefetch on that route 3) route ACME to dedicated small-model variant (lower mem). Which one can we action ASAP?

mike-sre: Reduce batch_size -> fastest. ops, can you patch routing or runtime config to cap batch at 32 for that pool? That should cut peak alloc. Also enable quick fallback to model-x-small for that customer.

ops-oncall: Patching now. CLI: ```redwood route update --pool infer-pool-7 --config max_batch_size=32 --route acme-customer --fallback model-x-small``` Applying with 30s TTL.

infra-bot: core-collector: core dump uploaded to s3://redwood-core-dumps/1749991234/infer-worker-7-core.tgz (uploader=ops-oncall). Diagnostic bundle enqueued.

carla-eng: I'll pull the core once it's available. If kselector v2 is the culprit we should rollback the kernel selection change or gate it under runtime flag.

raj-infra: Also recommend toggling off kv-prefetch for streaming routes: ```redwood feature-set update --route acme-customer --disable kv_prefetch``` That avoids early allocation spike while we debug.

emily-support: CS informed customer of a temporary routing change and reduced batch. They saw immediate reduction in 5xxs in the first 2m.

mike-sre: Good. Next steps: carla to reproduce locally with a load test matching ACME's QPS/context length; raj to gather full heap and nvml logs; ops to keep fallback in place until we validate. We'll create a dedicated postmortem if root cause ties to kselector rollout.

carla-eng: Assigning this to me. I'll try to repro with the same model, quant config, and kselector v2 in a controlled env. ETA 3h for initial repro attempt; will update here.

ops-oncall: Keeping the changed route config; I'll extend TTL to 2h and monitor. Alert if restart rate > 1/min.

emily-support: Thanks team — I joined CS call, customer on reduced throughput for now and ok with the workaround. I'll update stakeholder thread and open a postmortem ticket once we know root cause.

mike-sre: If anyone finds quick indicators for auto-detecting this pattern (prefetch mem ramp -> restart), add to runbooks. Tag me when the postmortem ticket is created.

infra-bot: monitor: alert suppression set for infra:infer-pool-7 (2h) by ops-oncall.

emily-support: closing the immediate escalation; we'll keep this thread for updates. Thanks all.
